messages:
Sharma P.: hey security — got an email that looked like a vpn password reset, clicked the link to see what it was. forwarding the original message now :grimacing:
Sharma P.: headers and link pasted below — i did NOT enter any creds but the page asked for corporate AD and showed a logo.
SecBot: phish-intake created INC-2026-452. auto-checking indicators... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Dana L.: @Sharma P. thanks for the report. did you enter anything or give MFA? any screenshots?
Sharma P.: no creds, an initial redirect to `https://vpn.redwood-secure-login.com/reset` then a subpage that asked for email + AD password + push. browser showed a cert warning for a moment. attaching headers:
```
From: "vpn-admin@redwood.com" <vpn-admin@redwood.com>
Received-SPF: fail (sender IP not in SPF record)
Authentication-Results: dkim=none; spf=fail; dmarc=fail
Received: from mail-45-67-89.example.net (45.67.89.123)
Message-ID: <CA+abc123@example.net>
Subject: Redwood VPN — immediate password reset required
```
Sharma P.: i saved the html but not sure how to upload here, can send to secure-uploads if needed.
Mike R.: @Sharma P. good call not to type creds. @Dana L. @Elliot (sec) can you run quick IOC on that sending IP and the domain? also check cloud-idp for any recent failed logins for Sharma.
Elliot (sec): ran SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks -> SPF fail, DKIM absent, DMARC policy none. IP 45.67.89.123 resolves to a cheap hosting provider in EU. quick url sandbox verdict (detonate): `vpn.redwood-secure-login.com/reset` -> suspicious (credential-harvest form). no malware drop, no payload. captured form fields: `email`, `password`, `mfa_method`. screenshot attached in ticket. :eyes:
SecBot: IOC scan results: domain vpn.redwood-secure-login.com -> matches 2 previous phishing reports in open intel feeds; IP flagged by Spamhaus SBL.
Dana L.: containment checklist: 1) force logout for Sharma + revoke active SSO sessions 2) rotate any API/service tokens Sharma used in last 24h (if any) 3) block domain at gateway/proxy and add to firewall denylist 4) create block rule in secure-web-filtering. @Helpdesk Bot please run step 1 now. :lock:
Helpdesk Bot: initiated SSO session revoke for Sharma P.; all active sessions invalidated (ticket TKT-3341). MFA re-enroll email sent.
Sharma P.: got notified, MFA prompt returned on my laptop. thanks.
Mike R.: quick audit ask: check KMS logs for any key access from 45.67.89.123 or related hostnames in the last 48h. unlikely but need to confirm no decryption requests. also check vault/secretsmanager access and service account auth logs.
Elliot (sec): checked KMS audit -> no requests from that IP or related userids. no suspicious get/decrypt calls. I also queried cloud provider IAM logs for suspicious token usage -> none.
Dana L.: RBAC question from this: do we need any temporary role changes? not for this case since no creds were given. but we'll tighten phishing-sensitive roles' MFA enforcement next week (create action item).
Mike R.: creating follow-ups: 1) block domain + add to intel feeds (done) 2) add this sample to sandbox corpus 3) user-awareness email to all staff with indicators and screenshots 4) sim campaign for next month targeted at similar lures.
Sharma P.: would you recommend rotating company-wide certs or KMS keys? i did see the cert warning briefly.
Elliot (sec): short answer: no rotation needed for KMS or company TLS certs. the cert warning was likely because the phishing host had a mismatched/lets-encrypt cert. rotate KMS only if audit shows any use of service account creds from impacted host (not the case). log this justification in the incident ticket.
Dana L.: i'll write the post-incident summary and send the awareness note. classify this as phishing — user clicked but no compromise. closure criteria: session revoke, domain blocked, sample ingested, awareness mail sent, training scheduled.
SecBot: incident INC-2026-452 updated: status=mitigated, severity=low, actions_completed=5, owner=Dana L.
Mike R.: thumbs up. can we also log this under security phishing tracker and mark Sharma P. for follow-up training?
Dana L.: yes — added to tracker and scheduled a 1:1 awareness touchpoint. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
Sharma P.: appreciate the fast help, will forward any similar mails to you immediately.
